title: Comments of C. Susan Holcomb re the proposed construction package of the Valley Link Transmission Line under ER26-1633.

documents.name: DocBatch261029-0012.pdf
documents.text:
,




    ORIGINAL
Federal Energy Regulatory Commission
888 First Street, N.E.
Washington, D.C. 20426


Re: Docket # ER26-1633-000


May 1, 2026


To Whom It May Concern:


Regarding Docket # ER26-1633-000 (the Valley Link Transmission Line) and understanding
the evaluation of the project is based upon Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland
Interconnection) "PJM" determination of projected. need, please consider these comments
in connection with alternative project options.


With the objective of being less costly and having significantly less impact on the
environment, land use and landowner impact, one option to be explored should be
development of one or more natural gas power plants in proximity to the PJM service area.
There are several natural gas providers in that area for which a lateral line connection could
be completed with dramatically less impact on the environment, land use, landowners, and
scenic views, and likely less costly.


A second option would be natural gas plants co-located with the large number of data center
sites within or in near proximity to the PJM service area. One statistic indicates there are
nearly 600 data centers in northern Virginia alone. Excess power generated at many data
centers could go into the grid for additional supply.


By siting a nuclear power plant and constructing 115 miles of a 765kV electric transmission
line to provide additional power to the PJM service area creates a near maximum amount of
impact to rural Virginia, farmers, landowners, natural resources, migratory bird flyways,
native American cultural resources, areas of current economic poverty levels, scenic
resources, potential threatened and endangered species, a significant number of wetlands
and water bodies and more. Reduction in property values and usage impacts of private
lands are created with this siting option. As you are well aware residents of all of the affected
Virginia counties are in sincere opposition to the proposed plan. Please also consider their
quality of life and potential health impacts from the generation of non-ionizing radiation
created by the transmission line.
 All of the affected areas mentioned above could be avoided by more selective siting of power
generation facilities creating a vast reduction in miles of electric transmission, possibly a
reduction in construction and maintenance costs, and certainly visual impacts.
Please urge PJM to consider alternatives to the proposed construction package of a nuclear
power plant, 115 miles of 765kV power line corridor and a large substation. And to select a
vastly less impactful option.


Thank you for your consideration.




C. Susan Holcomb
4005 West Chapel Drive
Goochiand, Virginia, 23063
